findings.evidence: template/scripts/publication_queue.py `_touches_openspec_change` (diff lines 575-583) hardcodes `origin/main`. It ignores the configured `main_branch`, which `required_check_state_for_ref` does read. It also assumes the admitted head object exists in the admitting checkout. A coordinator or legacy `admit` run without the fetched head, or in a project whose main is not `main`, raises instead of returning the quick-task identity. That contradicts the spec scenario 'Genuine quick task'. Design D4 says the head is 'listed from git at the admitted head', but does not mention this prerequisite. Tests that mock `_admission_handoff` would not catch it.
findings.summary: The managed predicate can make genuine quick-task admission fail. `_touches_openspec_change` runs `git merge-base <head> origin/main` and raises QueueError if that fails. It is the only evidence for classifying a candidate as quick when there is no managed state file.

findings.evidence: template/scripts/publication_state.py `required_check_state_for_ref` (diff lines 1038-1041). The docstring says 'Every unusable observation ... is `unknown` with an explicit cause'. `project_publish.wait_for_pr_checks`, `finish_task` and `rollout_preflight` call this function and expect a RequiredCheckState back, so a TOML or OS error would bypass their handling.
findings.summary: `required_check_state_for_ref` calls `read_platform_config(root)` outside the `_Unusable` handler. A malformed config therefore raises an arbitrary exception from a function whose contract is that every unusable observation returns `unknown` with a cause.
